mainTopic: Blood and הכשר לטומאה: blood splashed during שחיטה, and whether חבת הקודש works like contact with water
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a פסוק was needed to teach that we may benefit from the blood of פסולי המוקדשין. Next, דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that blood that spurts out at slaughter (דם קילוח) does not make seeds able to become טמא. A ברייתא then brings a מחלוקת about blood that splashed onto a gourd during שחיטה: רבי says the gourd is מוכשר, and רבי חייא says תולין. רבי אושעיא suggests relying on רבי שמעון, who holds that the שחיטה makes the animal susceptible, not the blood. רב פפא and רב אשי each explain the dispute and the word תולין differently. Each time, the גמרא shows how רבי שמעון and רבי חייא reach the same practical result, so רבי is outnumbered. Finally, ריש לקיש asks whether dry flour of a מנחה, open to טומאה only through חבת הקודש, passes טומאה on to a ראשון and a שני. רבי אלעזר answers from a פסוק, and the גמרא begins to show that his proof comes from an extra פסוק; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the verse was needed: we might have required burying the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a פסוק was needed. Since benefit from the fleece and labor of disqualified consecrated animals is forbidden, we might have thought their blood also needs burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since these animals are forbidden for shearing and for work, their blood should also need to be buried. So the פסוק teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by explaining why a פסוק was needed. Without it, we might have thought the blood of פסולי המוקדשין must be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefit from the wool (גיזה) and labor (עבודה) of these animals is forbidden. So we could have reasoned that their blood is also forbidden for benefit and must be buried, like other forbidden holy things. The פסוק shows that the blood is different and may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: It could enter your mind to say (introduces a mistaken first thought)
Shearing; the animal's fleece
Working with the animal
Burial, the way forbidden holy things are disposed of
So it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say these animals stop being holy. Their wool and labor stay forbidden. The only new point is that their blood is an exception and may be used.

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say:
since they are forbidden in fleece and labor,
phrases.notes: "They" means the disqualified holy animals the גמרא was just talking about.

phrases.english: their blood should require burial,
so it teaches us that it does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes an earlier discussion that asked why a פסוק was needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verse is needed to block a mistaken comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the fleece and labor are forbidden, the blood would also be forbidden and need burial
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that benefit from the blood is permitted

steps.title: Spurting blood does not make seeds susceptible to טומאה
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק "ודם חללים ישתה" to teach that blood that spurts out at slaughter (דם קילוח) does not make seeds able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "And drinks the blood of the slain" teaches that only blood of the killed animal counts. It excludes spurting blood, which does not make seeds susceptible to טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The school of רבי ישמעאל reads a פסוק to exclude spurting blood from making food able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food only becomes able to become טמא after a liquid such as blood touches it. The word חללים ("slain") points to blood of an animal that has been killed. Blood that shoots out under pressure while the animal is still alive does not count as "blood of the slain," so it does not make seeds susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: The slain; animals that have been killed
To exclude; except for
Blood that spurts out in a stream at slaughter
Makes food able to become טמא
Seeds; produce

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every blood released at slaughter counts for הכשר. This is the background for the next ברייתא, about blood splashed during שחיטה.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And drinks the blood of the slain"
excludes spurting blood,
which does not make seeds susceptible to impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new teaching about which blood counts for הכשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דם קילוח does not make seeds susceptible to טומאה

steps.title: Blood splashed onto a gourd: רבי and רבי חייא disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone slaughters and blood splashes onto a gourd. רבי says the gourd is מוכשר. רבי חייא says we leave it in doubt (תולין).
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if someone slaughters and splashes blood on a gourd, רבי says it became susceptible. רבי חייא says we leave it in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about whether blood splashed during שחיטה makes a gourd susceptible to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treats the splashed blood as real blood of slaughter, so the gourd is now susceptible. רבי חייא does not decide right away; he says תולין, 'we leave it pending.' The גמרא will soon give two explanations of what this means: 'wait and see' (step 6) or 'a lasting doubt' (step 9).

keyTerms.meaning: Splashed or sprayed
A gourd
It has become susceptible to טומאה
We leave it in doubt; we do not decide either way

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who slaughters and splashed blood on the gourd,
Rabbi says: it has become susceptible;
Rabbi Chiyya says: we leave it in doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the topic of blood of slaughter and הכשר to a practical case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: the gourd is מוכשר. רבי חייא: תולין.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: rely on רבי שמעון, who says slaughter makes the animal susceptible
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי and רבי חייא disagree, רבי אושעיא suggests relying on רבי שמעון. He holds that the שחיטה makes the animal susceptible, not the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: since רבי says it is susceptible and רבי חייא says we leave it in doubt, whom should we rely on? Let us rely on רבי שמעון, who used to say: slaughter makes it susceptible, not blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא faces the disagreement between two great authorities and proposes a third opinion to rely on: רבי שמעון's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing between רבי and רבי חייא, רבי אושעיא turns to רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that the act of שחיטה itself makes the animal susceptible, and the blood is not what does it. This moves the question away from the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; given that
We will rely on
The slaughter itself makes the animal susceptible to טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views: רבי (the gourd is מוכשר), רבי חייא (תולין), and רבי אושעיא's proposal to follow רבי שמעון: שחיטה מכשרת ולא דם.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is talking about what makes the animal itself susceptible. It is the שחיטה, not the blood. Don't read it as saying the animal can never become טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
Since Rabbi says it has become susceptible,
and Rabbi Chiyya says we leave it in doubt,
on whom shall we rely?

phrases.aramaic: בֹּאוּ וְנִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Come and let us rely on the words of Rabbi Shimon,
for Rabbi Shimon would say:
slaughter makes it susceptible, and not blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵאַחַר שֶׁרַבִּי אוֹמֵר הוּכְשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the מחלוקת in step 3 by proposing to rely on a third view
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אושעיא proposes following רבי שמעון: שחיטה מכשרת ולא דם.

steps.title: רב פפא: The dispute is only when the blood was wiped off
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that when blood stays on the gourd for the whole שחיטה, everyone agrees it makes the gourd susceptible. The dispute is only when the blood was wiped off between cutting the first and second סימן. רבי holds that שחיטה lasts from beginning to end, so even early blood counts as דם שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that if the blood is on the gourd from the beginning to the end of the שחיטה, it makes the gourd susceptible. They argue only when the blood was wiped off between one סימן and the other. רבי holds that שחיטה exists from beginning to end, so this is blood of שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains exactly where רבי and רבי חייא (from step 3) disagree, and gives רבי's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is narrowed to one situation: blood splashed on the gourd early, then was wiped off before the cutting was finished. רבי sees the whole cutting process as שחיטה, so blood from any moment of it is דם שחיטה. That kind of blood makes food susceptible to טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes (windpipe or food pipe) cut in שחיטה
Was wiped off
Makes food able to become טמא
Blood of slaughter, which makes food susceptible to טומאה
שחיטה counts from the first cut to the last

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי and רבי חייא argue about every splash. When the blood stays on until the end, they agree. They argue only when it was wiped off in the middle.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
All agree that where the blood is present
from the beginning to the end,
everyone agrees that it makes it susceptible.
Where they disagree is when the blood was wiped off
between one siman and the other siman.
phrases.notes: The two סימנים are the windpipe and the food pipe. The blood was wiped off after the first was cut but before the second.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סָבַר: יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף,
phrases.english: Rabbi holds: slaughter exists from beginning to end,
and this is blood of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the dispute in step 3 and explains exactly what רבי and רבי חייא argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood present from start to end makes the gourd susceptible according to all. If it was wiped off between the סימנים, רבי still says it does, because the whole process is שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי חייא's view and the meaning of 'we leave it in doubt'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא holds that שחיטה is only the final moment, so blood from before then is just blood of a wound. 'We leave it in doubt' means we wait to see whether blood is still on the gourd when the שחיטה is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא holds that שחיטה exists only at the end, so this is blood of a wound. What does 'we leave it in doubt' mean? We leave the matter pending until the שחיטה is finished. If blood is still on the gourd at the end of the שחיטה, it makes the gourd susceptible. If not, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי חייא's side of the argument. It also explains his word תולין, 'we leave it in doubt.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חייא, only the moment the שחיטה is completed counts as שחיטה. Blood that came out before that is דם מכה, wound blood, which does not make food susceptible. So תולין is not real uncertainty. It means waiting: blood still there at the end is דם שחיטה, and blood wiped off before then is not.

keyTerms.meaning: שחיטה counts only at its completion
Blood of a wound, which does not make food susceptible
We leave it pending and wait to see
The completion of the slaughter

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya holds:
slaughter exists only at the end,
and this is blood of a wound,
And what does "we leave it in doubt" mean?
We leave the matter pending until the slaughter is finished:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִיתֵיהּ לְדָם בְּסוֹף שְׁחִיטָה מַכְשִׁיר,
phrases.english: if the blood is there at the end of the slaughter, it makes it susceptible,
and if not, it does not make it susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא סָבַר: אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's explanation by giving the other side, רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only blood still present at the completion of the שחיטה makes the gourd susceptible. Blood wiped off before then does not.

steps.title: How can רבי חייא be joined with רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אושעיא meant by 'let us rely on רבי שמעון.' רבי שמעון says slaughter blood never makes food susceptible, but רבי חייא says it can, when the blood stays until the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did רבי אושעיא mean by 'Come, let us rely on the words of רבי שמעון'? According to רבי שמעון the blood does not make the gourd susceptible, but according to רבי חייא it does!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's statement from step 4. רבי שמעון and רבי חייא don't seem to agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא treated רבי שמעון as a way to settle the dispute in favor of רבי חייא. But רבי שמעון says the שחיטה itself, not the blood, makes the animal susceptible, so the blood never does anything. רבי חייא does say the blood counts if it stays to the end. So how are they on the same side?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us rely on

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי ״בֹּאוּ וְנִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״?
phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "Come and let us rely on the words of Rabbi Shimon"?
According to Rabbi Shimon, it does not make it susceptible,
while according to Rabbi Chiya, it does make it susceptible!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״בֹּאוּ וְנִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With רבי חייא's view now clear, the גמרא goes back to רבי אושעיא's statement in step 4 and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's suggestion to rely on רבי שמעון to decide the dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון says slaughter blood never makes food susceptible, while רבי חייא says it sometimes does. So רבי שמעון does not seem to support רבי חייא.

steps.title: In the wiped-off case they agree, so רבי is outnumbered
steps.stepSummary: In the case where the blood was wiped off, רבי שמעון and רבי חייא both say the gourd is not susceptible. So רבי is one opinion against two, and one opinion does not stand against two.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case where the blood was wiped off, at least, they are equal to each other. This master says it does not make it susceptible, and that master says it does not. So רבי is alone, and the words of one do not stand against two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי שמעון and רבי חייא agree in the exact case under dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון and רבי חייא disagree in general. But in the wiped-off case, the only case רבי and רבי חייא argue about, both rule 'not susceptible.' That gives two opinions against רבי's one, so the הלכה follows the majority. This is why רבי אושעיא could rely on רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: They are equal to each other (they reach the same result)
'Master,' used here for each of the two sages

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: One sage's view does not stand against two

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא: if the blood stays on the gourd until the end of the שחיטה, all agree it is susceptible. If it was wiped off between the סימנים, רבי חייא and רבי שמעון both say it is not, so together they outnumber רבי. רב אשי (next step) reads רבי חייא differently.

phrases.english: In the wiped-off case, at least, they are equal to each other:

phrases.aramaic: מָר לָא מַכְשִׁיר, וּמָר לָא מַכְשִׁיר,
phrases.english: this master says it does not make it susceptible, and that master says it does not make it susceptible,
phrases.notes: The two 'masters' are רבי שמעון and רבי חייא.

phrases.english: so Rabbi is one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and the words of one do not stand in the place of two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by narrowing the agreement to the wiped-off case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing: the two sages agree only in the specific case being disputed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון and רבי חייא hold different views, so רבי שמעון cannot help decide in favor of רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the wiped-off case both rule 'not susceptible,' so together they outnumber רבי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a sage can be counted as support for an opinion if he reaches the same result in the case at hand, even when his reasoning is different.

steps.title: A second reading: 'we leave it in doubt' means forever
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says 'תולין' means a permanent doubt. רבי חייא is unsure whether שחיטה runs from start to finish or is only the end, so in the wiped-off case we neither eat the gourd nor burn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'We leave it in doubt' means forever. In the case where the blood was wiped off, רבי חייא is unsure whether שחיטה lasts from beginning to end or is only the end. What does 'we leave it in doubt' mean? We don't eat it and we don't burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different explanation of רבי חייא's word 'תולין' from the one in step 6. He says it is not 'wait and see' but a doubt that can never be settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, 'תולין' meant we wait to see if blood is still on the gourd at the end of the שחיטה. רב אשי says that in the wiped-off case רבי חייא simply doesn't know which view of שחיטה is right. So the gourd stays doubtful forever. It might be טמא תרומה, so we can't eat it, and it might be טהור, so we can't burn it.

keyTerms.meaning: We leave it hanging in doubt.
It was wiped off (the blood came off the gourd).
He is truly unsure about it.
We neither eat it nor burn it (the rule for doubtful תרומה).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 6. There 'תולין' meant waiting to see what happens. Here רב אשי says 'תולין' is a doubt that never gets settled.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"We leave it in doubt" means forever,
and when it was wiped off,
Rabbi Chiyya is unsure about it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף,
phrases.english: whether slaughter lasts from beginning to end,
or slaughter is only at the end.
And what does "we leave it in doubt" mean?
We do not eat it and we do not burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of 'תולין' instead of רב פפא's reading in steps 5-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the wiped-off case רבי חייא has a permanent doubt, so the gourd is neither eaten nor burned.

steps.title: How can רבי חייא be grouped with רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: On רב אשי's reading, רבי שמעון says the gourd is not susceptible, while רבי חייא is only in doubt. So how could רבי אושעיא say 'let us rely on רבי שמעון'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'come, let us rely on the words of רבי שמעון' mean? For רבי שמעון the blood does not make the gourd susceptible, but for רבי חייא it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's reading by pointing to רבי אושעיא's statement from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא's words suggest there is a clear dispute that רבי שמעון can settle. On רב אשי's reading, רבי שמעון says 'not susceptible' while רבי חייא says 'maybe.' These are two different positions, so it's unclear how relying on רבי שמעון helps.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes food able to become טמא.
A doubt.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי ״בֹּאוּ וְנִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״?
phrases.english: And what does "come, let us rely on the words of Rabbi Shimon" mean?
According to Rabbi Shimon, it does not make it susceptible,
while according to Rabbi Chiyya, it is a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״בֹּאוּ וְנִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's reading from step 9 using רבי אושעיא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's suggestion to rely on רבי שמעון, as understood on רב אשי's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubt is not the same as 'not susceptible,' so רבי שמעון doesn't seem to side with רבי חייא.

steps.title: On burning they agree, so רבי is outvoted
steps.stepSummary: On the question of burning, רבי שמעון and רבי חייא give the same result: neither burns the gourd. So רבי is alone against two.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the matter of burning, at least, they are the same. According to this Sage we don't burn it, and according to that Sage we don't burn it. So רבי is one, and the words of one do not stand against two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that רבי שמעון and רבי חייא agree in practice on one point: don't burn the gourd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון doesn't burn because the gourd was never made susceptible. רבי חייא doesn't burn because it might be טהור. Their reasons differ, but the practical result is the same. So רבי, who would burn it, stands alone against two.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning, which is what we do with טמא תרומה.
They are equal to each other (they reach the same result).

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: One opinion does not stand against two.

steps.whyThisMatters: Two sages can count as agreeing for the הלכה even when their reasons are different, as long as the practical result is the same.

phrases.english: Regarding burning, at least, they are equal to each other:
according to this Sage we do not burn it,
phrases.notes: The standard printed גמרא has ומר, in round brackets. The corrected wording is the word in square brackets, וּלְמָר, "according to this Sage."

phrases.english: and according to that Sage we do not burn it.
So Rabbi is one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: and the words of one do not stand against two.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון and רבי חייא hold different positions, so רבי אושעיא's statement makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: On burning, both say don't burn, so they form a majority against רבי.

steps.title: What רבי חייא means: neither eat nor burn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up רבי חייא's ruling on רב אשי's reading: in a case like this the gourd is left in doubt and is neither eaten nor burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what he means: in a case like this we leave it in doubt. We don't eat it and we don't burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב אשי's approach by spelling out what רבי חייא's ruling means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי is outvoted on burning, the practical ruling is רבי חייא's. The gourd stays doubtful: it can't be eaten, because it might be טמא, and it can't be burned, because it might be טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means.
In a case like this.

steps.whatToRemember: On רב אשי's reading, a gourd whose שחיטה blood was wiped off partway stays doubtful forever. It is neither eaten nor burned, and רבי's view to burn it is outvoted two against one.

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying:
in a case like this, we leave it in doubt:
we do not eat it and we do not burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by restating רבי חייא's ruling in practical terms.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In such a case the gourd is left in doubt: not eaten and not burned.

steps.title: Does dry flour of מנחות pass on levels of טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether dry flour of a מנחה, which is open to טומאה only because it is holy, can pass טומאה on to a ראשון and a שני, or only becomes פסול itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש asked: dry flour of מנחות, do we count a ראשון and a שני with it, or not? Maybe holiness only works to make the flour itself פסול, but not to count a ראשון and a שני. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. ריש לקיש asks how far the special holiness of מנחה flour goes in passing on טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food normally becomes open to טומאה only after liquid touches it. Dry מנחה flour never got wet, yet its holiness alone lets it become טמא. The question is whether that holiness only lets the flour itself become פסול, or also lets it pass טומאה down the chain, ראשון then שני, like regular food.

keyTerms.meaning: A dry part of the flour that the oil did not reach.
Flour offerings brought in the בית המקדש.
First and second levels of טומאה.
Special regard for holy things, which makes them able to become טמא even without liquid.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked:
the dry portion of meal offerings,
do we count with it a first and a second level,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: or do we not count with it a first and a second level?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מַהְנְיָא חִבַּת הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְאִפְּסוֹלֵי גּוּפֵיהּ,
phrases.english: When regard for holiness works, it works to make the thing itself פסול,
but to count a first and second level with it, no?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: צָרִיד שֶׁל מְנָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how far holiness reaches in making things open to טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether dry מנחה flour, open to טומאה only through חבת הקודש, passes טומאה on to a ראשון and a שני.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק to answer ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל' to show that only food that came in contact with water is made susceptible to טומאה. Dry flour that never touched water would then not count further levels of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Come and hear. The פסוק says 'Of all food that may be eaten...' This teaches that food that came in contact with water is made susceptible, and food that did not come in contact with water is not made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר tries to answer ריש לקיש's question from step 13 using a פסוק. His point is that food never touched by water is not fully made ready for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש asked whether dry flour, open to טומאה only because it is holy, can make a ראשון and a שני. רבי אלעזר answers from the פסוק that only food that touched water counts as made ready for טומאה. Dry flour never touched water, so it should not pass טומאה down the levels; it only becomes פסול itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Was made ready (susceptible) to receive טומאה
Food that has come in contact with water
The process that makes food able to become טמא, normally contact with water or other liquids

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Come and hear,
"Of all food that may be eaten, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:34. The rest of the פסוק says 'on which water comes, it shall be טמא.'

phrases.english: food that comes in contact with water is made susceptible,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּמַיִם – לֹא הוּכְשַׁר.
phrases.english: food that does not come in contact with water is not made susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer ריש לקיש's question from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Dry flour susceptible only through חיבת הקודש does not make a ראשון and a שני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 11:34, 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל', read as: only food that came in contact with water is made susceptible.

steps.title: Surely ריש לקיש knows that rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבי אלעזר's proof. Does ריש לקיש really not know the basic rule that food needs contact with water?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רבי שמעון בן לקיש does not know the rule of 'food that comes in contact with water'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's proof. The rule he quoted is so basic that ריש לקיש could not have been asking about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that normal food needs contact with water to become susceptible. If that were the whole answer, ריש לקיש would never have asked. So the proof seems to miss the point of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a doubtful, challenging question)
He does not hold / does not accept

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
does not know the rule of food that comes in contact with water?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's proof from 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof only restates a basic rule ריש לקיש surely knew, so it cannot answer his question.

steps.title: What ריש לקיש was really asking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains ריש לקיש's real doubt. He was asking whether חיבת הקודש counts the same as contact with water, or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי שמעון בן לקיש was really asking: is חיבת הקודש like food that came in contact with water, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes clear what ריש לקיש's question actually was. This shows why a basic rule alone cannot answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש knew that food normally needs water. His question was whether the special holiness of a מנחה (חיבת הקודש) is a full replacement for water, so the flour would make a ראשון and a שני. The פסוק about water does not settle that, so רבי אלעזר's proof looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: The special regard for holy things, which makes holy food open to טומאה even without contact with water
He is asking / his question is
Is similar to / has the same status as

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not asking whether dry flour can become טמא at all; holiness already makes it able to. He is asking whether that holiness lets it pass טומאה further down, the way food that touched water does.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish is asking:

phrases.aramaic: חִבַּת הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּאוֹכֶל הַבָּא בְּמַיִם דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: is regard for holiness like food that came in contact with water,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection of step 15. By spelling out ריש לקיש's real doubt, it shows that רבי אלעזר's proof from step 14 misses the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש was unsure whether dry food can pass on טומאה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש was unsure whether חיבת הקודש has the same force as contact with water.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns from an extra פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. He was not just quoting the basic rule. He learns from extra wording in the פסוקים: since one פסוק already teaches about water on seeds, why is 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל' needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר too is learning from the extra words of the פסוקים. Since it is already written 'And when water is put on seed', why do I need 'Of all food that may be eaten'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר's proof comes from a seemingly extra פסוק. It ends by asking what that extra פסוק is there to teach, setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that food needs water is already taught by 'וכי יותן מים על זרע'. So the second פסוק, 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל', must be adding something new. רבי אלעזר will use that extra פסוק to answer ריש לקיש's real question about חיבת הקודש; the explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra, seemingly unneeded wording in the פסוקים, used to learn something new
Since / after all
Why do I need it? (asking what an extra source teaches)

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns רבי אלעזר's proof from a basic rule into a real derivation, so it can still answer ריש לקיש's question.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר נָמֵי מִיִּתּוּרֵי קְרָאֵי קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar too is speaking from the extra wording of the verses,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב ״וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע״,
phrases.english: since it is written: "And when water is put on seed,"
why do I need "Of all food that may be eaten"?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר נָמֵי מִיִּתּוּרֵי קְרָאֵי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אלעזר's proof from step 14 against the objection in steps 15-16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source is an extra פסוק, not the basic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר simply quoted the basic rule that food needs water.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר learns from the extra פסוק 'מכל האוכל אשר יאכל', which must teach something beyond the basic rule.
